models.name: Claude Fable 5
strengths: Highest SWE-bench Verified on the board (~95.5% self-announced, ~95% independent)
Anthropic's most capable widely-available model; built for long-horizon autonomous agents
1M-token context at standard pricing
Always-on thinking; high-resolution vision
weaknesses: Most expensive model here: $10/$50 per M — exactly 2x Opus 4.8
Reported availability/export restrictions (was briefly pulled offline June 2026)
Requires 30-day data retention; not available under zero-data-retention
Overkill and overpriced for routine work
models.verdict: Use only for the hardest reasoning or overnight autonomous agent runs where its capability edge justifies paying 2x Opus.

models.name: Claude Opus 4.8
strengths: Top generally-available coding model (88.6% SWE-bench Verified)
Flagship Opus intelligence at half Fable's price ($5/$25)
1M context at flat rate; optional Fast mode
GPQA Diamond 93.6% (third-party reported)
weaknesses: Premium-priced for high-volume/bulk workloads
Slower and pricier than Sonnet 5 for most production agents
Beaten on paper by the restricted Fable/Mythos tier
models.verdict: The default pick for demanding coding, agentic, and reasoning work when you want top-tier quality without Fable's premium.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5
strengths: ~85% SWE-bench Verified at a fraction of Opus's price — best coding value right now
1M context; default model on Free/Pro plans
Intro pricing $2/$10 per M through Aug 31 2026
Built to run agents cheaply at scale
weaknesses: Intro price rises to standard $3/$15 on Sept 1 2026
Below Opus/Fable on the hardest coding and reasoning tasks
Some third-party benchmark figures for it are inconsistent across sources
models.verdict: The cost-efficient workhorse: most of Opus's coding ability at ~40% of the cost — the daily driver for personal projects.

models.name: GPT-5.5
strengths: Previous OpenAI flagship; still a strong all-rounder
SWE-bench Verified 81.9% (reported), GPQA Diamond 93.6%
LMArena text Elo 1475; 1M-token API context
weaknesses: Superseded by GPT-5.6 at the same price — usually no reason to pick over Sol/Terra now
Sources conflict on its coding metric (Verified 81.9% vs SWE-bench Pro 58.6%)
Weaker multimodal performance
models.verdict: Only choose over GPT-5.6 if you've already validated a pipeline on it; otherwise 5.6 dominates at equal cost.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Pro (Preview)
strengths: Current Gemini flagship; top-tier reasoning (GPQA 94.3), tied at the top of the AA Intelligence Index
Strong agentic coding (SWE-bench Verified 80.6)
Cheap for a frontier model ($2/$12 up to 200k tokens); 1M context, strong multimodal
weaknesses: Price doubles to $4/$18 above 200k-token prompts
Still a Preview SKU (may change)
Trails top Claude models on coding
models.verdict: The best-value frontier coder outside Anthropic — reach for it for hard reasoning, big multimodal context, or the Google ecosystem.

models.name: DeepSeek V4-Pro
strengths: Near-Opus coding quality (80.6% SWE-bench Verified) at a fraction of the price
Open weights (MIT); self-hostable
1M-token context; cache-hit input extraordinarily cheap (~$0.0036/M)
weaknesses: Top SWE-bench score is 'Think Max' mode (slower/pricier in tokens)
Benchmark figures from secondary aggregators, not a primary vendor card
Trails best closed models by ~8 pts on coding
models.verdict: The best-value open-weight coder — frontier-ish quality without frontier prices, and self-hostable to avoid lock-in.

models.name: Kimi K2.6
strengths: Elite agentic coding — 80.2% SWE-bench Verified; ties GPT-5.5 on SWE-bench Pro
1T-param MoE (32B active), open weights
Built for long-horizon multi-step agent tasks
weaknesses: Pricier output than the cheapest DeepSeek/Qwen tiers
Third-party host prices vary widely ($1.15-$2.15 blended)
262K context, below the 1M-token models
models.verdict: Reach for it when building coding agents that run long multi-step tasks and you want open weights that rival top closed models.

models.name: Llama 4 Maverick
strengths: Very cheap for its quality via hosts like Fireworks/Together/Groq
1M-token context; open weights, widely available
MMLU-Pro 77.1, SWE-bench 74.2 (secondary-sourced)
weaknesses: No single official Meta list price — cost varies 20%+ by host
Trails top open coders (DeepSeek/Kimi/Qwen) on SWE-bench
Benchmarks from secondary aggregators
models.verdict: A cheap open-weight generalist with huge context — good for bulk work and long documents on a widely-hosted model.

models.name: o4-mini
strengths: Cheap reasoning model: AIME 2025 92.7% (beats o3), SWE-bench Verified 68.1%
GPQA 81.4%; reasons over images (multimodal)
~10x cheaper inference than o3 for near-o3 results
weaknesses: Retired from the ChatGPT UI (Feb 2026); API-only
Older o-series generation, overshadowed by the GPT-5.x reasoning line
GPQA figure may not be the Diamond subset
models.verdict: A cost-efficient math/reasoning pick via API, but the GPT-5.6 line is the modern default.

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
strengths: Cheapest Claude ($1/$5 per M)
Fastest tier; ideal for classification, routing, extraction, high-volume simple tasks
~$37 to process 10,000 support tickets (Anthropic's own example)
weaknesses: Smaller 200K context vs 1M on the larger models
Not for hard reasoning or long-horizon agentic work
No published SWE-bench/GPQA figures from reliable sources
models.verdict: Reach for it when volume and speed matter more than peak intelligence — cheap bulk classification, routing, and extraction.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
strengths: Flagship of the GPT-5.6 line; tops the Artificial Analysis Coding Index
SWE-bench Pro 64.6% and Terminal-Bench 2.1 88.8% (agentic-coding leader)
GPQA Diamond 94.6%; strong long-context recall (MRCR 91.5%)
Marketed as OpenAI's best model for cybersecurity/long-horizon tasks
weaknesses: OpenAI did NOT publish SWE-bench Verified, AIME, or MMLU-Pro for it
Chain-of-thought reasoning means higher latency and token usage
Higher output price ($30) than Claude Opus
models.verdict: Pick this if you're in the OpenAI/Codex ecosystem and want their strongest coding-agent and reasoning tier; cost is secondary.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Terra
strengths: Balanced mid-tier: half Sol's price with close performance
Terminal-Bench 2.1 87.4%, Coding Agent Index 77.4 (just under Sol)
Cost-per-task ~$0.55 vs Sol's ~$1.04; 1M context, strong long-context recall
weaknesses: OpenAI omitted GPQA, AIME, SWE-bench Verified, MMLU-Pro for this tier
Not as strong as Sol on the hardest agentic/security tasks
models.verdict: The default everyday GPT-5.6 pick: most of Sol's ability at half the price.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Luna
strengths: Cheapest 5.6 tier at $1/$6; cost-per-task just ~$0.21
Still competitive: Terminal-Bench 2.1 84.7%, Coding Agent Index 74.6
1M context
weaknesses: Weak long-context recall (MRCR 41.3% vs Sol's 91.5%) — avoid for large-doc tasks
No published GPQA/AIME/SWE-bench Verified/MMLU-Pro
models.verdict: Use for high-volume or budget coding/agent work where you don't need deep long-context recall.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash
strengths: Near-Pro reasoning (GPQA 92.2 per Artificial Analysis) at Flash speed
Fast (~278 output tokens/sec); 1M context
High spot on the AA Intelligence Index for its price class
weaknesses: Output price ($9) is high for a Flash tier
Only SWE-bench Pro (55.1) published, not SWE-bench Verified
Audio input billed higher
models.verdict: Use when you want most of Pro's smarts but need it fast and cheaper for high-volume chat, coding, or long-context work.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite
strengths: Cheapest Gemini ($0.10 in / $0.40 out)
1M-token context
Great for massive-scale simple tasks like classification and extraction
weaknesses: Lowest capability tier — not for reasoning or complex coding
Older 2.5 generation
Audio input billed higher
models.verdict: The rock-bottom-cost Gemini for huge-volume, low-complexity jobs.

models.name: Grok 4.5
strengths: xAI's newest flagship, pitched as 'Opus-class'; very token-efficient (~4x fewer output tokens than Opus 4.8)
Cheap output ($6/M) vs frontier peers; strong agentic coding (SWE-bench Pro 64.7%, Terminal-Bench 2.1 83.3%)
75% cache discount ($0.50 cached input); bundled into Cursor
weaknesses: xAI did NOT publish classic academic benchmarks (GPQA/AIME/MMLU/SWE-bench Verified) at launch
500k context is smaller than Gemini/Claude's 1M
Not available in EU at launch; preview-era figures may shift
models.verdict: The cheap frontier-class coder: reach for it when you want strong agentic coding at low, token-efficient cost.

models.name: DeepSeek V4-Flash
strengths: Rock-bottom price for a frontier-lineage model ($0.14/$0.28)
1M-token context
Cache-hit input near-free (~$0.0028/M) for repeated-prefix / agent workloads
weaknesses: The 'flash' tier trades some reasoning depth vs V4-Pro
No cleanly-sourced benchmarks for the flash tier specifically
models.verdict: Reach for it to process huge volumes of text or code cheaply when you don't need the absolute top reasoning tier.

models.name: Qwen3-Max
strengths: Qwen's flagship general model; top-tier on several coding/agent benchmarks per Qwen
256K context; batch API halves the price
Large open ecosystem
weaknesses: Newer Max releases moving closed-weight
Input price tiers up to $3/M past 128K tokens
No clean primary SWE-bench Verified number for this SKU
models.verdict: Qwen's do-everything flagship — pick it for top Qwen quality across reasoning and code when you can pay flagship rates.

models.name: Qwen3-Coder-Plus
strengths: Hosted, tuned coding model with up to 1M context
Context-caching discount available
Strong Qwen coding lineage
weaknesses: Tiered pricing climbs steeply past 32K tokens
Output at $5/M is not cheap-bulk territory
No clean primary SWE-bench figure for this exact SKU
models.verdict: Use for a managed Qwen coding endpoint with very long context when you don't want to self-host the open weights.

models.name: Qwen-Turbo
strengths: Among the cheapest hosted models anywhere ($0.05/M input)
Thinking mode available at $0.5/M output
weaknesses: Small/fast model — not for hard reasoning or agentic coding
Context window not clearly documented in the pricing table
models.verdict: Use for massive-volume simple tasks — classification, tagging, extraction, cleanup — where cost per token matters most.

models.name: Mistral Medium 3.1
strengths: Strong price-to-quality mid-tier from a European (EU-hosted) vendor
Good all-round coding and text model
weaknesses: Not open-weight (Medium tier is commercial)
No cleanly-sourced benchmark for this version
models.verdict: A solid EU-based mid-tier — reach for it when data residency or a European provider matters and you want balanced cost/quality.

releases.title: GPT-5.6 (Sol/Terra/Luna) reaches general availability
releases.summary: Three-tier family (Sol $5/$30, Terra $2.50/$15, Luna $1/$6) tops the Artificial Analysis Coding Index; previewed June 26 behind a US-government access list.

releases.title: xAI releases Grok 4.5
releases.summary: 'Opus-class' token-efficient coding/agentic model at $2/$6 per M — far cheaper than Opus 4.8 — bundled into Cursor; not available in EU at launch.

releases.title: Anthropic redeploys Claude Fable 5
releases.summary: Fable 5 came back online after the US government lifted a June 12 export-control order that had pulled it offline — an AI-governance flashpoint.

releases.title: Anthropic launches Claude Sonnet 5
releases.summary: Cheaper agent-focused model, near-Opus quality; intro pricing $2/$10 per M through Aug 31 (then $3/$15), 1M context, default on Free/Pro.

releases.title: Open-weight wave: DeepSeek V4 preview, GLM-5.2, Qwen3-Coder-Next
releases.summary: A cluster of 1M-token open-weight coding models landed, pressuring closed-model pricing — including the compact 80B/3B-active Qwen3-Coder-Next.

releases.title: Moonshot ships Kimi K2.7 Code
releases.summary: Open-weight coding model claiming +21.8% over K2.6 on its own Kimi Code Bench v2 — continued fast iteration in Chinese open-weight coders.

releases.title: Google ships Gemini 3.5 Flash
releases.summary: Fast Flash-tier model with near-Pro reasoning (GPQA ~92%), 1M context, ~278 tok/s, at $1.50/$9 per M.

releases.title: Claude Opus 4.8
releases.summary: Flagship Opus tier at $5/$25 per M, 1M context, 88.6% SWE-bench Verified — the strong coding/agentic default below Fable's price.

releases.title: DeepSeek V4-Flash and V4-Pro
releases.summary: Open-weight (MIT) 1M-context models at rock-bottom prices; V4-Pro hits ~80.6% SWE-bench Verified with near-free cache-hit input.

releases.title: OpenAI introduces GPT-5.5
releases.summary: Prior flagship at $5/$30 per M, 1M context, 81.9% SWE-bench Verified and LMArena Elo 1475 — now largely superseded by GPT-5.6 at equal cost.

releases.title: Moonshot releases Kimi K2.6
releases.summary: 1T-param MoE (32B active) open-weight agentic coder at 80.2% SWE-bench Verified, built for long-horizon multi-step tasks.

releases.title: Claude Haiku 4.5
releases.summary: Cheapest/fastest Claude at $1/$5 per M, 200K context — built for high-volume classification, routing, and extraction.

benchmarks_legend.swe_bench: SWE-bench Verified — % of real-world GitHub issues resolved end-to-end (agentic coding). Note: several 2026 models published only SWE-bench Pro, a different/harder variant, so their Verified cell is null.
benchmarks_legend.gpqa: GPQA Diamond — % correct on graduate-level, Google-proof science reasoning questions.
benchmarks_legend.aime: AIME — % on advanced high-school competition math (American Invitational Mathematics Examination).
benchmarks_legend.mmlu_pro: MMLU-Pro — % on a harder, multi-discipline knowledge and reasoning benchmark.
benchmarks_legend.lmarena_elo: LMArena text Elo — human head-to-head preference rating (higher = preferred more often).

notes: Data snapshot 2026-07-12. Pricing is verified against official vendor pricing pages (standard tier, USD per 1M tokens) — treat it as the reliable layer. Benchmarks are directional: most come from third-party aggregators (Artificial Analysis, Vellum, llm-stats, vals.ai), not primary vendor cards, and several 2026 models publish only agentic evals (SWE-bench Pro, Terminal-Bench) that don't map to SWE-bench Verified — those cells are left blank rather than cross-filed. A blank (—) means 'not reliably sourced,' never a guess. Note: Sonnet 5 shows its current intro price ($2/$10; rises to $3/$15 on Sept 1, 2026). Re-verify any single benchmark against a primary leaderboard before betting real spend on it.
